Welcome! I'm so glad you're here. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. As part of our conversation today, I'd like to use the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, or EPDS, to better understand your emotional well-being during this significant time in your life. The EPDS is a helpful tool that allows us to have a more informed conversation about how you're feeling and coping with the challenges of new motherhood.

Please know that everything we discuss is confidential and a safe space for you to share your feelings. Our goal is to provide you with the support you need during this period. The EPDS consists of 10 questions that I'll be asking you, and it should only take a few minutes to complete. I'll be asking you about your experiences over the past 7 days.

Let's get started. Here's the first question: How have you been feeling in terms of laughter and enjoying things - have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things as much as you normally would?

To be honest, I haven't been laughing much at all lately. It's not that I don't find things funny, it's just that everything feels so overwhelming with the baby and taking care of myself. I used to enjoy little things, like watching a funny movie or hanging out with friends, but now it all just feels like too much. I mean, I'll see something funny, but it's not like it used to make me laugh out loud or anything. It's more like a faint smile, if that makes sense. I don't know, it's just not the same as it was before having the baby.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

As much as I always could, Not at all 
Most of the time 
Not quite so much 
Definitely not as much 

I would say "Not quite so much".
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

As much as I ever did 
Definitely as much 
Not quite so much 
Not at all 

I would say "Not quite so much". To be honest, it's been hard to find things to look forward to lately. Taking care of the baby is a lot of work, and it feels like there's not much time for anything else. When I do try to think about things I used to enjoy, it just doesn't feel as exciting or fun as it used to.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes, most of the time 
Yes, some of the time 
Not very often 
No, never 

I would say "Yes, some of the time". I do feel like I'm not doing enough or that I'm not a good enough mother, and when something goes wrong, like the baby cries a lot or doesn't sleep well, I tend to blame myself. It's like I'm always thinking I could be doing something differently, and it's hard not to take it personally. It's not all the time, but it's definitely some of the time.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

No, not at all 
Hardly ever 
Yes, sometimes 
Yes, very often 

I would say "Yes, sometimes". I do worry a lot about the baby's health and safety, even when there's no real reason to. I'll be lying in bed at night thinking about all the things that could go wrong, and it's hard to shake those thoughts off. It's not all the time, but it's definitely happened a few times this week.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

No, not at all 
No, not much 
Yes, sometimes 
Yes, quite a lot 

I would say "Yes, sometimes". There have been a few times when I've felt really overwhelmed and anxious, and it's hard to explain why. I'll be holding the baby and suddenly feel this wave of fear or panic, and I don't know what's causing it. It's not like I'm thinking anything specific is wrong, it's just this feeling of being on edge. It's happened a few times, but not all the time.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes, most of the time I haven't been able to cope 
Yes, sometimes I haven't been coping as well as usual 
No, most of the time I have coped quite well 
No, I have been coping as well as ever 

I would say "Yes, sometimes I haven't been coping as well as usual". Some days it feels like everything is just too much, and I'm not sure how I'm going to get through the day. But other days are okay, I manage to get by. It's just the caring for the baby, and the household, and everything else... it can feel really overwhelming at times.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes, most of the time 
Yes, sometimes 
Not very often 
No, not at all 

I would say "Yes, sometimes". To be honest, I've been having trouble sleeping a lot lately, and it's not just because of the baby waking up. Even when the baby is asleep, I've been lying awake thinking about things and feeling really down. It's like my mind is racing and I just can't turn it off. It's not every night, but it's happened a few times this week.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes, most of the time 
Yes, quite often 
Not very often 
No, not at all 

I would say "Yes, quite often". I have been feeling really sad and down a lot lately. It's like there's this cloud following me around, and I just can't seem to shake it off. It's not all the time, but it's often enough that it's starting to feel normal. I'll be doing something, like feeding the baby or taking a shower, and suddenly I'll just feel this overwhelming sadness. It's hard to explain.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes, most of the time 
Yes, quite often 
Only occasionally 
No, never 

I would say "Only occasionally". I've cried a few times this week, usually when I felt really overwhelmed or just felt like I wasn't doing enough as a mother. It's not like I'm crying all the time, but when I do, it's usually because something has triggered this feeling of sadness or frustration. It's not constant, but it's happened a few times, and it's been really unsettling.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

Yes, quite often 
Sometimes 
Hardly ever 
Never 

I would say "Never". No, that thought has never crossed my mind. I'm just really struggling to cope with everything and feeling really overwhelmed, but I would never think of harming myself. I'm just trying to get through this and be a good mom to my baby.

This new mother is experiencing significant emotional distress, including feelings of sadness, guilt, and anxiety. She reports difficulty enjoying activities, coping with responsibilities, and sleeping due to racing thoughts and feelings of overwhelm. Despite these challenges, she denies any thoughts of self-harm.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 16, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>The patient states 'Not quite so much' and elaborates that it's been hard to find things to look forward to, indicating a decrease in enjoyment. This aligns with 'Definitely less than I used to' in the guidelines.</sym>, <sym>The patient indicates they blame themselves 'some of the time' when things go wrong, aligning with the chosen guideline option.</sym>, <sym>The patient selected 'Yes, sometimes' and described experiencing worry about the baby's health and safety, indicating moderate anxiety.</sym>, <sym>The patient indicates they feel scared or panicky 'Yes, sometimes', describing instances where they felt overwhelmed and anxious without a clear reason.</sym>, <sym>the guideline 'Yes, sometimes I haven't been coping as well as usual'.</sym>, <sym>The patient selected 'Yes, sometimes' and elaborated that they've had trouble sleeping due to feeling down and racing thoughts, aligning with the 'Yes, sometimes' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient selected 'Yes, quite often' as their response and elaborated that they have been feeling sad and down frequently, which aligns with the EPDS guideline for a score of 2.</sym>)
**Reasoning:** The patient's EPDS score of 16 indicates a high risk for <med>postpartum depression</med>. She reports <sym>persistent sadness</sym>, <sym>loss of pleasure</sym>, and <sym>sleep disturbances</sym> linked to her mood. She also experiences <sym>feelings of guilt</sym> and <sym>anxiety</sym>, which are common symptoms of <med>Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>. Although she denies any <sym>suicidal ideation</sym>, her symptoms warrant urgent referral to a <med>mental health specialist</med> for further evaluation and support. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>mental health specialist</med>
2. Encourage sleep hygiene practices
3. Offer emotional support and validate her feelings
4. Discuss coping strategies and stress management techniques
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 16: **Postpartum Depression Screening Summary**

**Main Symptoms and Concerns:**

1. Reduced ability to enjoy things (Q1, Q2)
2. Self-blame and guilt (Q3)
3. Anxiety and panic (Q4, Q5)
4. Difficulty coping with responsibilities (Q6)
5. Sleep disturbances linked to mood (Q7)
6. Frequent feelings of sadness and misery (Q8)
7. Occasional crying spells (Q9)

**Patterns and Screening Significance:**

The patient reports a consistent pattern of low mood, reduced enjoyment, and anxiety. She expresses feelings of guilt and inadequacy as a mother, and often feels overwhelmed by her responsibilities. Sleep disturbances are linked to her emotional state. These symptoms are relevant to postpartum depression and anxiety.

**Risk Factors:**

1. Persistent sadness and loss of pleasure
2. Sleep difficulties linked to mood
3. Feelings of worthlessness or guilt
4. Anxiety and panic
5. No indication of self-harm or suicidal thoughts (Q10)

**Screening Observation Summary:**

The patient screens positive for symptoms consistent with postpartum depression and anxiety. She reports significant emotional distress, including low mood, anxiety, and feelings of guilt and inadequacy. While she denies any thoughts of self-harm or suicidal ideation, her symptoms indicate a need for further evaluation and potential support. Monitoring and follow-up are recommended to assess the severity of her symptoms and determine the best course of action.
